name: moving-line

frames.best_why: Frame 1 shows the rule at its longest beside the opening chapter; later frames catch it mid-retraction.

tagline: A hairline rule down the page shortens as the reader scrolls.
summary: A vertical rule sits left of a column of story chapters and retracts from the top as the page scrolls, its last drawn point following the reader. The chapters carry dates, headings, copy and paired photos.
appearance: A dark page column of travel chapters, each with a small grey date, a bold heading, a paragraph and two wide landscape photos side by side. A pale hairline rule runs down the left edge of the column, faint at the top and a little brighter toward the bottom.
behaviour: As the reader scrolls, the vertical line shortens from its top end, the remaining length tracking page progress and settling with a spring when scrolling stops. The chapter content scrolls past as normal.
demo_content: Three chapters headed Into the clouds, Ridge walking and The way down, labelled Day 1 to Day 3 with alpine photos.
search_phrases: vertical line that shrinks as you scroll
scroll progress indicator on the left
timeline rule tied to page position
story chapter layout with a progress bar
line that follows scrolling down a page
reading progress marker for long articles
thin rule shrinking between photo sections
use_when: A long photo story or article wants a quiet marker of how far the reader has travelled.
avoid_when: Content is not roughly 1567px tall, or you need progress that reads at a glance.
customise: Chapters go in as children. The rule's height, the spring stiffness and the two-stop gradient are fixed in the source and need editing.
weight_why: A single SVG path whose length one scroll-linked spring updates.

a11y.note: Decorative rule with no reduced-motion check; the demo's photos all use empty alt text.

issues: The rule is hard-wired to 1567px, so it drifts out of step with content of any other length.
The rule is so faint against the dark page that progress is easy to miss.
polish_why: Clean editorial layout and photos, but the progress rule is barely visible and tied to one height.
title: Scroll Progress Line
